name: Mem0 OSS
one_line: One ADD-only extraction call per add() over the payload, 10 neighbour memories and the last 10 messages; zero-LLM hybrid read (dense + BM25 + entity boost, additive fusion).

arch.product.t: Python library (Memory / AsyncMemory) plus a TypeScript OSS SDK with the same pipeline, a self-hosted FastAPI REST server with a Next.js dashboard, and an OpenAI-compatible chat proxy. The managed Platform is a separate product reached through MemoryClient.
arch.product.e: read: pyproject.toml:7; mem0/memory/main.py:487,2193; mem0-ts/package.json:3; mem0-ts/src/oss/src/memory/index.ts:25,72; server/main.py:120-143; mem0/proxy/main.py:23; mem0/client/main.py

arch.truth.t: The vector-store payload (text, hash, lemmatised text, scope ids, timestamps, attributed_to) is the only copy of a memory. SQLite holds an ADD/UPDATE/DELETE history log with old and new text, and a rolling window of the last 10 raw messages per scope; no full raw-turn archive on the default infer=True path.

arch.stores.t: Qdrant by default (local path /tmp/qdrant) out of 25 configurable backends; a memory collection plus a sibling '<collection>_entities' collection in the same backend; SQLite history.db (history + messages tables). The REST server defaults to pgvector.
arch.stores.e: read: mem0/vector_stores/configs.py:9,14-38; mem0/configs/vector_stores/qdrant.py:16; mem0/memory/main.py:422-424,559-580; mem0/configs/base.py:42-45; server/main.py:122-131

arch.graphdb.t: External graph store (Neo4j etc.) removed from OSS in v3; graph memory is now Platform-only. OSS keeps an entity collection whose linked_memory_ids back-pointers act only as a retrieval boost.

arch.scope.t: At least one of user_id, agent_id or run_id is required on add, search, get_all and delete_all; search and get_all take them only inside filters. Identity keys in caller metadata are stripped so metadata cannot place a memory in another scope; optional actor_id narrows queries.

write.entry.t: add(messages, user_id/agent_id/run_id, metadata, expiration_date, infer=True, memory_type, prompt); messages may be a string, dict or list. The caller decides whether one turn or a whole session is one add(). infer=False stores each non-system message verbatim with no LLM call.

write.receipt.t: Synchronous: add() returns after the vector insert. Batch insert with a one-by-one fallback; only records confirmed stored are returned; raises VectorStoreError if none persisted. History and entity-linking failures are logged and swallowed.

write.roles.t: Both user and assistant messages go to the extractor (system messages too, as 'system:' lines); each fact carries attributed_to user or assistant. Agent-only scope (agent_id without user_id) appends an agent-perspective suffix. role and actor_id are stored only on the infer=False path.

write.firewall.t: Not found: no injection or poisoning check on input or extracted facts. Only input-shape validation and identity-key stripping from metadata.

write.governance.t: Per-memory expiration_date (YYYY-MM-DD) hides expired rows from search and get_all unless show_expired; no PII redaction, consent or retention policy. Anonymous PostHog telemetry is on by default (MEM0_TELEMETRY), with secret-like config fields redacted.

segment.unit.t: No segmentation: whatever the caller passes to one add() call becomes one extraction call.

segment.rule.t: None; no boundary detection. Session continuity comes only from the rolling 10-message window keyed by the user/agent/run scope string.

extract.calls.t: 1 LLM call per add() (default gpt-5-mini, JSON mode) with a static system prompt of about 33,900 characters (roughly 8.5k tokens); plus one vision call per image when enable_vision is set. Procedural path is also 1 call.

extract.facts.t: The only derived layer: self-contained 15-80 word facts (up to 100 when detail-rich) from both speakers, ADD-only, with relative dates resolved against an Observation Date.

extract.dates.t: The prompt converts relative to absolute dates against an Observation Date, but OSS never passes one: timestamp is refused and the Observation Date defaults to the run date, so replayed history is dated wrongly; live use is correct.

extract.neighbours.t: Top 10 existing memories (by one embedding of the whole payload) re-numbered '0'-'9', and the last 10 messages truncated to 300 characters each. The model's linked_memory_ids are never read; the Summary and Recently Extracted slots are always empty in OSS.

extract.failure.t: An LLM call failure raises LLMError (no silent empty list), but an unparseable JSON response is logged and treated as 'nothing extracted': messages are saved and [] is returned.

graph.entities.t: spaCy (en_core_web_sm) rule-based mentions typed PROPER, QUOTED, TOPIC or IDENTIFIER, with NER label allow/deny lists; no LLM. Run in batch over all new facts in an add().

graph.resolution.t: Merge on exact normalised text (lists up to 10,000 entities in scope) or top-1 cosine >= 0.95; otherwise a new entity. Scoped by user/agent/run.

graph.edges.t: None between entities; only entity-to-memory back-pointers (linked_memory_ids).

time.fields.t: created_at (now, UTC) and updated_at, plus optional expiration_date; no event or validity time. A caller-supplied metadata created_at survives into the payload but does not reach the extractor.
time.fields.e: read: mem0/memory/main.py:1035-1037,828-829; inferred: main.py:363-365 strips identity keys only

time.update.t: Extraction is ADD-only: old and new facts both survive with no supersession or contradiction check. Manual update(memory_id, text) rewrites in place and logs UPDATE in history.

time.dedup.t: MD5 exact-text match against the 10 retrieved neighbours and within the batch; semantic near-duplicates are left to the extractor prompt.

derive.session.t: None in OSS; the prompt's Summary slot is always passed empty.

derive.profile.t: None in OSS. User Profiles v1 (get/generate profile jobs) exist only on the Platform client.
derive.profile.e: read: mem0/client/main.py:807-955; grep finds no profile code in mem0/memory/

derive.entity.t: Not found; entity rows hold only text, type and linked ids.

derive.background.t: None in OSS; all work is inline in add(). The chat proxy runs add() in a daemon thread.

derive.forget.t: Delete by id, delete_all by scope (batched 1,000), reset, and expiry hiding. No decay: project.update(decay=True) raises a Platform-only error.

index.embed.t: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small by default; facts and entities embedded in batches.

index.lexical.t: spaCy-lemmatised text stored per memory; on Qdrant a fastembed Qdrant/bm25 sparse vector (disabled if fastembed is missing). 15 of 25 backends implement keyword_search; others fall back to semantic only with a warning.

index.vector.t: Qdrant default; 25 backends (pgvector, Chroma, Pinecone, Milvus, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Redis, Valkey, FAISS, S3 Vectors, Turbopuffer and others).

read.rewrite.t: Not found; the query is only trimmed and lemmatised.

read.analysis.t: spaCy lemmas (for BM25 and query-length-adaptive sigmoid) and up to 8 query entities; a regex temporal detector only triggers a Platform notice.

read.legs.t: Dense top max(4 x top_k, 60) (80 at default top_k 20); a keyword leg with the same limit; entity leg searches the entity store (top 500 per entity, sim >= 0.5). Only dense candidates are scored: keyword and entity hits outside the dense pool are dropped.

read.temporal.t: reference_date is refused in OSS; the Platform's temporal-intent scoring is documented but not in the clone.

rank.fusion.t: Additive: semantic + sigmoid-normalised BM25 + entity boost (max 0.5), divided by the best reachable sum (1, 1.5, 2 or 2.5 depending on which signals fired), capped at 1.

rank.rerank.t: Optional, needs both a reranker config and rerank=True per call: Cohere, sentence-transformer, ZeroEntropy (zerank-1), HuggingFace or LLM reranker; on failure the fused order is kept.

rank.gate.t: Semantic score threshold 0.1 applied before fusion, so BM25 or entity signals cannot rescue a weak dense match; no abstain signal.

answer.shape.t: A list of memory dicts (text, score, scope ids, attributed_to, metadata; score_details when explain=True); the caller formats. The proxy joins memory texts into one 'Relevant Memories/Facts' line.

answer.size.t: Vendor runs: mean 6,956 tokens per LoCoMo query at top_200 (Platform). OSS default top_k is 20 facts, roughly 0.4k-2k tokens.
answer.size.e: doc: docs/core-concepts/memory-evaluation.mdx:131; README.md:49; read: mem0/memory/main.py:1397; inferred size from 15-80 word facts

answer.prompt.t: MEMORY_ANSWER_PROMPT ships in the clone and is used by the chat proxy; it asks for concise answers and tells the model not to say no information was found (no abstention). Benchmark answer prompts live in the separate memory-benchmarks repo.

eval.best.t: 92.5 (1,425/1,540) at top_200 and 91.8 at top_50, vendor, managed Platform with proprietary optimisations.

eval.outside.e: our notes (OmniMemEval results.md; BENCHMARKS_UPDATE_2026-10-02); not re-checked in this pass

eval.models.t: Not stated for the Platform runs ('production-representative model stack'). The harness defaults to gpt-4o answerer and judge; GPT-5 answerer and judge are stated only for the OSS LongMemEval extraction-model comparison.
eval.models.e: doc: docs/core-concepts/memory-evaluation.mdx:140,190-191; mem0ai/memory-benchmarks README (CLI options; OSS with Different Extraction Models)

eval.rigour.t: Harness is public (mem0ai/memory-benchmarks, empty submodule here) with full 1,540 q, top-k cutoffs 10/20/50/200 and a stated ±1 judge interval; but headline numbers come from the Platform, models are unstated and category scores average across cutoffs.

cost.write.t: 272 (one add() per session) to 5,882 (turn by turn) extraction calls, each re-sending the ~8.5k-token system prompt; plus per add() one payload embedding, one fact batch embedding and one entity batch embedding.

cost.read.t: 0 LLM calls; 1 query embedding, 1 batch embedding for up to 8 entities, a dense search, a keyword search and up to 8 entity searches. An LLM reranker, if enabled, adds calls.

cost.where.t: Hosted by default (OpenAI gpt-5-mini and text-embedding-3-small); spaCy and fastembed BM25 run locally; local LLMs and embedders (Ollama, HuggingFace, etc.) are configurable.

trust.provenance.t: Each fact carries attributed_to (user or assistant), and history logs ADD/UPDATE/DELETE with actor and role; there is no link from a memory to its source turn or message id.

trust.erasure.t: delete removes the vector and strips entity links, but the SQLite history row keeps the deleted text (old_memory, is_deleted=1) and the last 10 raw messages persist; only reset() drops everything.

trust.auth.t: Library has none. The REST server offers JWT, hashed API keys, an admin key and a rate limiter (AUTH_DISABLED switch), but the authenticated principal is not bound to user_id, so any key can read or write any scope.

trust.sharing.t: Scope ids only (user/agent/run combinations, optional actor_id filter); no ACLs or cross-agent sharing model.

keep: Zero-LLM read path with explainable additive scoring (explain=True returns each signal)
Anti-hub entity penalty: 1 / (1 + 0.001(n-1)^2) on the entity boost
Integer re-numbering of neighbour memories in the extraction prompt to stop UUID hallucination
Batch-phased write: one embed batch for facts, one for entities, one insert, with per-item fallbacks
Raises on LLM call failure instead of returning an empty list
avoid: linked_memory_ids requested from the model, then discarded; the prompt even promises UUIDs while integer ids are sent
Observation date is the run date in OSS, so replayed history gets wrong absolute dates
Candidates come only from the dense leg; exact-hash dedup only; ADD-only keeps stale facts
Delete leaves the old text in the SQLite history table; REST auth not bound to user scope
Chat proxy passes user_id top-level to search(), which the OSS Memory rejects (inferred breakage)

extras.t: Stores each non-system message verbatim with role and actor name, no LLM call; the only raw-turn layer.
memory_type='procedural_memory' with agent_id writes one LLM summary of an agent's execution history; flagged for removal.
With enable_vision, image parts are described by the LLM before extraction.
Identity keys (user_id, agent_id, run_id, actor_id) in caller metadata are dropped with a warning; immutable on update.
Config-level or per-call prompt text is appended as highest-priority Custom Instructions; the server can generate them from a use-case description with one LLM call.
Builder has a same-language/script section for CJK and mixed languages, but OSS never enables it and project.update(multilingual) raises.
Agent-only scope reframes facts as agent knowledge while keeping attributed_to as the true source.
AND/OR/NOT plus eq, ne, in, nin, gt(e), lt(e), contains, icontains and wildcard, translated per backend.
Returns semantic, BM25, entity, raw and normalised scores per result.
Sigmoid midpoint 5-12 and steepness 0.7-0.5 chosen by lemmatised query length so long queries do not saturate.
Retrieves with the last 6 messages as query, prepends memories to the user turn and adds the conversation in a background thread.
mem0-ts 3.3.1 ports the additive prompt, BM25 lemmatisation, scoreAndRank and the entity store; 26 vector-store adapters (adds in-memory and Cloudflare Vectorize).
16 integration packages (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Vercel AI SDK, n8n, Zapier, Strands and others) plus Python and Node CLIs.
FastAPI server with request logging, X-Request-ID, API-key management, admin-only /configure and a Next.js dashboard.
PostHog events on init/add/search; with telemetry on, a separate 'mem0migrations' vector collection is created.
OSS raises or prints notices for Platform-only features (timestamp, reference_date, decay) and at scale thresholds: 2,000 memories, top_k >= 50, queries over 2 s.
Platform runs a separate temporal-metadata pass at write and query temporal-intent scoring at read, and offers User Profiles v1; none of this is in OSS.

specialities.name: Single-call ADD-only extraction
specialities.t: One JSON-mode call per add() sees the payload, 10 neighbours and the last 10 messages and only emits new facts; nothing is updated or deleted, which removes the UPDATE/DELETE decision step entirely.

specialities.name: Integer-id anti-hallucination mapping
specialities.t: Neighbour UUIDs are swapped for '0'-'9' before the prompt and mapped back, so the model cannot invent ids.

specialities.name: Normalised additive multi-signal fusion
specialities.t: Semantic, sigmoid BM25 and entity boost are summed and divided by the maximum reachable score for the signals that fired, giving a bounded, explainable score with no LLM.

specialities.name: Anti-hub entity boost
specialities.t: Entity boost = similarity x 0.5 x 1/(1 + 0.001(n-1)^2), where n is the number of memories linked to the entity, so hub entities stop flooding results; max over query entities.

specialities.name: Batch-phased write pipeline
specialities.t: Facts embedded in one batch, entities deduplicated globally then embedded and searched in batches, one bulk insert; each phase falls back to per-item work on failure.

specialities.name: Rolling per-scope message window
specialities.t: SQLite keeps exactly the last 10 raw messages per scope string, used as pronoun/coreference context for the next extraction.

specialities.name: Token-budget reporting
specialities.t: Vendor results report accuracy against context tokens at top-k cutoffs 10/20/50/200 (92.5 at top_200 vs 91.8 at top_50).

token_economy.t: Each memory is a 15-80 word fact; OSS search defaults to top_k 20 (roughly 0.4k-2k tokens), while vendor runs use top_200 at a mean of 6,956 tokens on LoCoMo (91.8 vs 92.5 at top_50). Write prompts stay bounded: 10 neighbours, last 10 messages cut to 300 characters each. The ~8.5k-token static system prompt is re-sent on every add(); no explicit prompt caching in code (it sits first, so provider prefix caching may apply, inferred).
token_economy.e: read: mem0/configs/prompts.py:468-944,631,965-972; mem0/memory/main.py:922,928-933,1397; doc: docs/core-concepts/memory-evaluation.mdx:129-134; grep finds no cache_control in mem0/

speed.t: Read: zero LLM; entity-store searches run on a 4-thread pool; one query embedding plus one batch for entities. Write: one LLM call, batch embeddings, bulk insert. AsyncMemory wraps the sync steps in asyncio.to_thread (no extra parallelism within an add()). Slow-query notice above 2 s. Vendor p50 latency 0.88 s on LoCoMo (Platform).
